Hi, I’m Sara. I’m an HR manager in Stockholm. Are you here for the talk about benefits?
Yes! I’m Andrea, Head of HR in Brazil. Benefits are one of my areas.
Great. So tell me: what is the most important benefit in Brazil?
The health plan, for sure. And the meal allowance. In Sweden?
Our public health system is good, so a health plan is less important. People want flexible hours and more paid time off.
Interesting. Here, candidates ask about remote work more than about a bonus.
Same in Sweden. Time is more valuable than money for young people.
And the best perk in your company?
Fika! A coffee break every afternoon, with cinnamon buns. It’s cheaper than a bonus, and people love it.

Hi, I'm Liam, and I'm an HR manager in Melbourne. Last year we asked our employees a simple question: which benefit is the most important for you? About six hundred people answered. The results surprised my boss. The most popular benefit was flexible hours, not the bonus. Remote work was second, and the health plan was third. The bonus was only fifth. Many people said: time with my family is more important than a little more money. So we changed some things. Now everybody has flexible hours, and we gave everybody two more days of paid time off. It was cheaper than a bigger bonus, and people are happier.

Hello, my name is Anjali, and last month I had two job offers. The first one was from a big bank. The salary was higher, and the bonus was bigger. But I had to be in the office five days a week, and the commute was more than an hour. The second offer was from a smaller company. The salary was a little lower, but it had remote work two days a week, flexible hours and a better health plan for my family. My father said: take the bank, it's safer. But I chose the smaller company. For me, time is the most valuable thing.
